لَبِدٌ (S, K) and ↓ لُبَدٌ , (S, A, L, K,) the former of which is preferable, accord. to A'Obeyd, (S,) (tropical:) One who does not travel, (S, L,) nor quit his abode, (S, * L, K,) or place, (A,) nor seek sustenance. (L, K.) Hence, (A,) the last of Lukmán's [seven] vultures [with whose life his own was to terminate] was called ↓ لُبَدٌ , (S, A, L, K,) because he thought that is would not go away nor die. (L.) Thus applied, it is perfectly decl., because it is a word not made to deviate from its original form. (S, L.) ―
-b2- Also ↓ لُبَدٌ A man who does not quit his camel's saddle. (L.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
